name: Training models better
gist: Using new techniques like reinforcement learning and preference optimization to train models that follow human judgment more closely.
explain: Why train models better? Because standard training methods break down when there is no single right answer, which is the reality of multimodal tasks. For most of the history of machine learning, training has been straightforward: show the model examples, it makes predictions, compare the prediction to labeled ground truth, and adjust the model to match the right answer. This works fine when there is one objectively right answer. But real-world multimodal tasks do not have a single right answer. A caption can be accurate but vague, or detailed but focusing on the wrong thing. A question can be answered correctly but unhelpfully. Different people would judge quality differently — one person wants brevity, another wants detail, a third wants emotional resonance. A single labeled correct answer cannot capture this variation. Standard training methods fail in this situation because they force a choice that does not exist. So researchers are developing better training methods — methods that work by learning from human preference and judgment, not from a single labeled answer, which means the model can produce outputs that different humans would actually prefer. Reinforcement learning and preference-based learning try to do this by letting humans rank or score different outputs, and then training the model to produce outputs that humans consistently prefer.

In the context of multimodal models, this is especially useful. Suppose your image captioning model outputs 'a dog sitting.' Is that right? Well, maybe — it's accurate, but the ground truth might be 'a tan dog sitting on a green grass lawn.' The first caption is not wrong, but the second is more detailed and specific. Or suppose your visual question answering model answers 'yes' to 'Is there a cat in the image?' when the image shows a cat but it's far in the background and blurry. Technically correct, but maybe not what the user wanted. Preference learning lets you say: I prefer detailed captions to vague ones, or I prefer answers that acknowledge uncertainty when the image is ambiguous. The model learns not just to get the right answer, but to get it in the right way.

The tools for this include reinforcement learning, where the model is rewarded for behaviors you like and discouraged from behaviors you don't. It also includes preference optimization, a newer technique where the model directly learns from pairs of outputs — 'I like this caption better than that one' — without needing an explicit reward function. This works because the model learns to chase the kinds of outputs humans prefer, which is more efficient than guessing at a reward formula. Some research applies these methods specifically to multimodal tasks, like training a model to generate image descriptions that humans consistently pick as better. Humans prefer detailed, natural-sounding descriptions that actually capture what's in the image because those are more useful for understanding the picture, so training the model to match those preferences makes it more practical. Other applications include training to avoid hallucinating details in visual question answering. The result is a model that is not just accurate but aligned with what humans actually want.

papers.title: BaseReward: A Strong Baseline for Multimodal Reward Model
papers.contribution: BaseReward achieves state-of-the-art performance on MM-RLHF-Reward Bench, VL-Reward Bench, and Multimodal Reward Bench, demonstrating practical utility when integrated into real-world reinforcement learning pipelines for enhancing MLLMs.

papers.title: Breaking the SFT Plateau: Multimodal Structured Reinforcement Learning for Chart-to-Code Generation
papers.contribution: Breaks the SFT plateau on a 3-million chart-code pair corpus from arXiv, demonstrating substantial improvements from reinforcement learning.

papers.title: DaVinci: Reinforcing Visual-Structural Syntax in MLLMs for Generalized Scientific Diagram Parsing
papers.contribution: DaVinci significantly outperforms existing open-source MLLMs and surpasses leading proprietary models like GPT-5 and Claude-Sonnet-4 on scientific diagram parsing.

papers.title: Importance Sampling for Multi-Negative Multimodal Direct Preference Optimization
papers.contribution: Consistently improves multimodal alignment across five benchmarks by incorporating semantic-aware, multi-negative sampling in preference-based learning.

papers.title: SPIKE-RL: Video-LLMs meet Bayesian Surprise
papers.contribution: Achieves consistent performance gains on five downstream benchmarks by enabling Video-LLMs to track beliefs and register surprise.

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Vision-Language Model via Reasoning Decomposition and Multi-Reward Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: The method improves visual reasoning without external supervisions and provides balanced training signals through self-rewarding multi-reward policy optimization.

papers.title: SophiaVL-R1: Reinforcing MLLMs Reasoning with Thinking Reward
papers.contribution: SophiaVL-R1-7B outperforms LLaVA-OneVision-72B on multiple benchmarks despite having 10x fewer parameters.

papers.title: TTS Can Speak in Any Style with Any Voice
papers.contribution: Supports zero-shot voice cloning with flexible natural-language style control and handles both Chinese and English in a single bilingual model, surpassing baselines in naturalness, controllability, and robustness while disentangling control factors.

papers.title: AVoCaDO: An Audiovisual Video Captioner Driven by Temporal Orchestration
papers.contribution: AVoCaDO significantly outperforms existing open-source models across four audiovisual video captioning benchmarks.

papers.title: Beyond Fixed Biases: Decoding the Role of Reasoning Uncertainty in MLLM Modality Conflicts
papers.contribution: The framework enables preference steering through data-efficient fine-tuning on boundary cases, improving robust preference alignment without internal vacillation.

papers.title: CFPO: Counterfactual Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
papers.contribution: Achieves 3.17%-6.25% improvements over RL baselines and 1.32%-2.13% over perception-aware methods on multimodal reasoning tasks without external reward models.

papers.title: Can Speech LLMs Think while Listening?
papers.contribution: Reasoning in text space improves speech LLM accuracy by 2.4x; entropy-based approach yields 4% accuracy gain on ARC-Easy under equivalent latency and DPO achieves 70% latency reduction.

papers.title: Chart Deep Research in LVLMs via Parallel Relative Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: The approach addresses training bottlenecks through parallel reward optimization and evaluation limitations through error-uniqueness-based benchmarking, advancing chart data intelligence.

papers.title: CogFlow: Bridging Perception and Reasoning through Knowledge Internalization for Visual Mathematical Problem Solving
papers.contribution: Contribute MathCog dataset with 120K+ perception-reasoning aligned annotations and achieve improved visual grounding in mathematical reasoning.

papers.title: DeAltHDR: Learning HDR Video Reconstruction from Degraded Alternating Exposure Sequences
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods with controllable attention ratio for adaptive inference costs and practical deployment via self-supervised learning.

papers.title: Do Audio LLMs Listen or Read? Analyzing and Mitigating Paralinguistic Failures with VoxParadox
papers.contribution: Improves Audio Flamingo 3 from 17.40% to 65.20% on VoxParadox and from 37.74% to 54.78% on MMSU paralinguistic subset.

papers.title: E-VAds: An E-commerce Short Videos Understanding Benchmark for MLLMs
papers.contribution: E-VAds-R1 achieves 109.2% performance gain in commercial intent reasoning with only a few hundred training samples.

papers.title: EEmo-Logic: A Unified Dataset and Multi-Stage Framework for Comprehensive Image-Evoked Emotion Assessment
papers.contribution: Achieves robust performance in emotion QA and fine-grained assessment on in-domain and cross-domain datasets, advancing machine empathy capabilities.

papers.title: Echo: Towards Advanced Audio Comprehension via Audio-Interleaved Reasoning
papers.contribution: Echo achieves superiority on audio comprehension benchmarks through audio-interleaved reasoning, confirmed efficient and generalizable across domains.

papers.title: EmotionThinker: Prosody-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Explainable Speech Emotion Reasoning
papers.contribution: Generates accurate emotion predictions with interpretable explanations grounded in fine-grained acoustic cues through deep reasoning approach.

papers.title: Empowering Small VLMs to Think with Dynamic Memorization and Exploration
papers.contribution: The method consistently improves small VLM performance across diverse domains by stabilizing the SFT-RLVR tradeoff.

papers.title: Evaluating and Rewarding LALMs for Expressive Role-Play TTS via Mean Continuation Log-Probability
papers.contribution: MCLP aligns well with human judgments of stylistic consistency and effectively improves style alignment between generated speech and role-play instructions.

papers.title: Fix Before Search: Benchmarking Agentic Visual Query Pre-processing in Multimodal Retrieval-augmented Generation
papers.contribution: Reveals critical vulnerabilities to visual imperfections and shows supervised fine-tuning enables compact models to achieve comparable or superior performance to larger proprietary models.

papers.title: Judo: A Juxtaposed Domain-oriented Multimodal Reasoner for Industrial Anomaly QA
papers.contribution: Surpasses Qwen2.5-VL-7B and GPT-4o on MMAD benchmark with enhanced domain knowledge and contextual reasoning.

papers.title: MARS-Sep: Multimodal-Aligned Reinforced Sound Separation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates consistent gains in text-, audio-, and image-queried separation on multiple benchmarks with improved semantic quality.

papers.title: MergeMix: A Unified Augmentation Paradigm for Visual and Multi-Modal Understanding
papers.contribution: Achieves dominant classification accuracy while improving generalization and alignment of MLLMs with training efficiency and stability.

papers.title: Mini-o3: Scaling Up Reasoning Patterns and Interaction Turns for Visual Search
papers.contribution: Naturally scales to tens of reasoning turns during inference despite training with six-turn upper bound; improves accuracy with increased reasoning turns.

papers.title: Native Active Perception as Reasoning for Omni-Modal Understanding
papers.contribution: Achieves positive test-time scaling where 7B OmniAgent outperforms 10x larger Qwen2.5-VL-72B on LVBench (50.5% vs 47.3%).

papers.title: Navigating Massive Visual Context in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Multimodal Memory Graph
papers.contribution: Consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance on diverse multimodal RAG benchmarks through structured memory and policy optimization.

papers.title: Omni-Perception Policy Optimization for Multimodal Emotion Reasoning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on MER-UniBench and substantially improves utilization and faithfulness scores, highlighting importance of sufficient and faithful omni-perception.

papers.title: Omni-Reward: Towards Generalist Omni-Modal Reward Modeling with Free-Form Preferences
papers.contribution: Omni-Reward introduces Omni-RewardBench (first omni-modal RM benchmark) and Omni-RewardData (248K general + 69K instruction pairs), achieving strong performance on multiple benchmarks.

papers.title: Perceptual Flow Network for Visually Grounded Reasoning
papers.contribution: Sets new state-of-the-art records on V* Bench (90.6%) and MME-RealWorld-lite (67.0%) with provable performance guarantees.

papers.title: R1-Reward: Training Multimodal Reward Model Through Stable Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: R1-Reward achieves 8.4% improvement on VL Reward-Bench and 14.3% on Multimodal Reward Bench, with further improvements as inference compute increases.

papers.title: RL makes MLLMs see better than SFT
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that RL reshapes visual representations fundamentally compared to SFT, proposing PIVOT recipe for building stronger vision encoders that outperform larger counterparts.

papers.title: Robust-U1: Can MLLMs Self-Recover Corrupted Visual Content for Robust Understanding?
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art robustness on corruption benchmarks and adversarial settings; analysis confirms visual recovery quality directly enhances reasoning.

papers.title: Synergizing Understanding and Generation with Interleaved Analyzing-Drafting Thinking
papers.contribution: Improves performance across understanding and generation benchmarks with strong transferability to various UVLM architectures.

papers.title: Thyme: Think Beyond Images
papers.contribution: Enables models to perform rich on-the-fly image manipulations and mathematical computations while maintaining high autonomy in deciding when and how to apply operations.

papers.title: Traceable Evidence Enhanced Visual Grounded Reasoning: Evaluation and Method
papers.contribution: Maintained transcription accuracy while achieving 0.685 F1 score on uncertainty tagging in degraded OCR and introduced TreeBench, a diagnostic benchmark.

papers.title: Unlocking the Essence of Beauty: Advanced Aesthetic Reasoning with Relative-Absolute Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: Improves backbone PLCC/SRCC metrics by 47.9%/34.8%, surpassing similar-scale baselines and enabling grounded aesthetic scoring and reasoning in unified framework.

papers.title: ViSurf: Visual Supervised-and-Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Large Vision-and-Language Models
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms standalone SFT, RLVR, and sequential pipelines across diverse benchmarks while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Video-STAR: Reinforcing Open-Vocabulary Action Recognition with Tools
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on HMDB-51, UCF-101, SSv2, Kinetics-400, and Kinetics-600, distinguishing fine-grained actions with computational efficiency while reducing cross-modal hallucination.

papers.title: Visual Jigsaw Post-Training Improves MLLMs
papers.contribution: Visual Jigsaw improves fine-grained perception, temporal reasoning, and 3D spatial understanding across images, videos, and 3D data without additional visual generative components.

papers.title: Wiki-R1: Incentivizing Multimodal Reasoning for Knowledge-based VQA via Data and Sampling Curriculum
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on Encyclopedic VQA (35.5% to 37.1%) and InfoSeek (40.1% to 44.1%), improving accuracy through curriculum learning.
